prompt: You're twelve years old and your parents finally let you sign up somewhere. Where do you start?

options.label: The wrestling club at the rec center
options.text: You spend two years getting thrown around a mat by kids twice your size, and slowly stop minding it.

options.label: The boxing gym above the laundromat
options.text: The old man who runs it doesn't say much, but he watches your hands like they're the only thing that matters.

options.label: A martial arts dojo
options.text: It's more bowing than fighting at first, but the patience it teaches you sticks around long after the belts stop mattering.

prompt: High school. Everyone has to be something. What are you?

options.label: Varsity wrestling
options.text: Two-a-days, cutting water weight before you know what a real cut even is, and a mat that never gets easier.

options.label: Track in spring, football in fall
options.text: You're not the biggest kid on the field, but nobody catches you either.

options.label: Skip the teams, study the tape instead
options.text: While everyone else is at practice, you're rewinding old fights frame by frame, trying to understand why, not just what.

prompt: You're eighteen and it's time to pick a real gym — the one that'll actually make you.

options.label: Ironside MMA — grinders and wrestlers
options.text: Nobody at Ironside cares how you look. They care whether you can survive top position for five straight rounds.

options.label: Golden Gate Boxing — a striking pedigree
options.text: The walls are covered in fight posters going back decades. They teach you to hit like it's a craft, not a tantrum.

options.label: Apex Grappling Academy — a jiu-jitsu factory
options.text: You lose. Constantly. For months. And then one day you don't, and you understand why they made you lose so much.

prompt: You're in the gym six days a week now. What's actually getting the work?

options.label: Pads, bag work, sparring — striking, striking, striking
options.text: Your hands and feet start moving before you consciously decide to throw anything.

options.label: Live grappling rounds, every single day
options.text: You start to feel positions before you see them — a hand on the hip that means a takedown is coming.

options.label: The weight room and the conditioning coach
options.text: Nobody claps for a good conditioning session. You do it anyway, because you've seen what round three does to people who don't.

prompt: Your first real amateur loss. The one that actually teaches you something.

options.label: Caught in a submission you never saw developing
options.text: You tapped, and then you watched the tape forty times trying to find the exact moment you gave your neck away.

options.label: Taken down and ground out for three rounds
options.text: You never got hurt badly, but you never got up, either. That gap between 'tough' and 'effective' becomes personal.

options.label: Out-boxed by someone with half your athleticism
options.text: He never looked fast. He was always exactly one step ahead of where you swung.

prompt: The last camp before you turn pro. Where do you put the final push?

options.label: Turn the intensity up and stop holding back
options.text: You spend the camp getting hit harder than you ever have, on purpose, so fight night doesn't surprise you.

options.label: Recovery, mobility, staying in one piece
options.text: You've watched too many prospects get hurt in camp and never get their shot. You're not going to be one of them.

options.label: A sports psychologist, twice a week
options.text: Half of it feels ridiculous. The other half is the only reason you're not panicking backstage anymore.
